\/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-family: georgia; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EQ1) Where are the different anatomical locations of the patient's problems and what are the different etiologic possibilities for them? Please chart out the sequence of events timeline between the manifestations of each of these problems and current outcomes.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA) The anatomical locations of the problems and their etiological possibilities :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe pain in the epigastrium could be because of MI, Gastritis, peptic ulcer etc.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere could be pancreatitis secondary to chronic alcohol consumption, gallstones, Hypertriglyceridemia, chronic smoking and high age.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn the Kidneys for Oliguria\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere could be pre renal AKI possibly due to the fluid loss that's occurring because of the pancreatitis or it could also be tubular injury in the kidneys due to Sepsis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe heart and lungs for SOB \u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe pancreatitis could cause pleural effusion by means of MODS\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe AKI could lead to volume overload and heart failure which eventually leads to the development of shortness of breath as a symptom.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe decrease\/difficulty in passing stools could be because of the pancreatitis causing paralytic ileus preventing normal bowel movement, or any intestinal obstruction, the former possibly due to any ischaemia or decreased blood supply or bacterial toxin induced. \u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ESequence of events\u003C\/b\u003E :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInitially the patient had the complaints of the bow leg deformity which was congenital\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe then gave a history of alcohol consumption and smoking for a chronic period of about 30 years.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe finally presented with the complaints of abdominal pain and distension, SOB, chest pain and decreased urine output since 3 days.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOutcomes after admission to the hospital :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eat day 2 of admission the urine output increased and there was a decrease in the SOB and pedal oedema.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt day 3 the patient was in Altered sensorium\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt day 4 dialysis was done for the patient\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt day 5 the patient gave complaints of bilious vomiting\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt day 6 Dialysis was again done for the patient.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt day 8 there was decrease in the abdominal pain and vomitings\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient has now been put on a schedule for hemodialysis due to his Renal failure.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQ2)\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EWhat are the pharmacological and non pharmacological interventions used in the management of this patient and what are the efficacy of each one of them?\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EA2) \u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003EThe \u003Cu\u003E\u003Cb\u003Enon pharmacological interventions\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E used in the treatment of the patient are :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Cspan\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E1. keeping the patient Nil by oral\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Cspan\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E2. Placing a ryles tube\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E3. And oxygenating the patient as and when required\u003C\/span\u003E.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe \u003Cu\u003E\u003Cb\u003Epharmacological interventions\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E used in this patient are :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. First and foremost replacing fluids intravenously seems to be the way forward as there is increased vascular permeability seen in pancreatitis which leads to decreased plasma volume as the days progress. This can lead to Shock and possible renal failure and subsequent decrease in the microvascular blood supply to the pancreas may lead to pancreatic ischemia and necrosis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. Antibiotics although prescribed here actually play no role for obvious reasons in pancreatitis that isn't caused by infectious agents.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Antibiotics haven't been proven to be efficacious in patients with acute pancreatitis as its an inflammatory process.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe following article gives us some insight regarding the same :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;P - 1097\u0026nbsp; with Severe Acute Panceatitis who were \nadmitted to the study institutions between January 1, 2009, and December\n 31, 2013, a retrospective cohort study of all consecutive patients.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EI- Of the 1097 patients with SAP, 850 (77.5%) received \u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"antimicrobial prophylaxis\"\u003Eantimicrobial prophylaxis\u003C\/span\u003E, and 21 (1.9%) had invasive pancreatic candidiasis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EC-The results suggest that \u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"antimicrobial prophylaxis\"\u003Eantimicrobial prophylaxis\u003C\/span\u003E may contribute to the development of invasive pancreatic candidiasis, and therefore, the routine use of \u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"antimicrobial prophylaxis\"\u003Eantimicrobial prophylaxis\u003C\/span\u003E for SAP may be discouraged\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EO - In multivariable logistic regression analysis, \u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"antimicrobial prophylaxis\"\u003Eantimicrobial prophylaxis\u003C\/span\u003E was significantly associated with the development of invasive pancreatic candidiasis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/30946245\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/30946245\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"post-sidebar\"\u003E\n\u003Cdiv class=\"post-sidebar-item post-share-buttons\"\u003E\n\u003Cdiv aria-owns=\"sharing-popup-Blog1-byline-5610282367859973641\" class=\"sharing\" data-title=\"\"\u003E\n\n\u003Cdiv class=\"share-buttons-container\"\u003E\n\n\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\n\n\n\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/30946245\/\"\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3. Tramadol has been given to the patient for the management of pain.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4. Zofer has been given to the patient to reduce the episodes of vomitings.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5. Pantop has been given to this patient to prevent excess acidic environment and gastritis and further damage to the pancreas.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6.Injections Of Furosemide were given to reduce the fluid overload in the patient.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E7. Patient was nebulized in order to provide relief for SOB and reduce the incidence of wheeze and crepts.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQa1) Added 17\/11\/2020 Mention the optimal diagnostic interventions in the \npatient done and that you may further order in a low resource setting to\n fathom the etiologic possibilities.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAa1)\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp; I would order for Routines such as hemogram to look for sepsis, RFT to assess the serum creatinine and blood urea levels\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan\u003E\u0026nbsp;as the patient was in renal failure, ABG shows metabolic acidosis due to renal failure\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan\u003E\u0026nbsp;The FLP shows hypertriglyceridemia\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI would order for a USG Abdomen to look for the cause of abdominal pain.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Right upper limb carotid doppler was done as the patient had right upper\n limb venous stasis and had feeble pulse which revealed complete \nocclusion of right radial \u0026amp; ulnar artery, and right distal large \nplaque extending to proximal ICA causing 50-70% stenosis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI would want to order for a CECT abdomen as it would aid in diagnosing the presence of any pancreatic necrosis, any pseudocysts, any calcifications etc. and that would aid in changing in our treatment strategy. \u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECase 2 :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia; font-size: large;\"\u003EA 55 year old male, shepherd by occupation, presented to the OPD with the chief complaints of fever (on and off), loss of appetite, headache, body pains, generalized weakness since 2 months, cough since 2 weeks and vomitings and pain abdomen since 2 days\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; Please chart out the \nsequence of events timeline between the manifestations of each of these \nproblems and current outcomes.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;A1) Anatomical locations of the patients problems and their etiological possibilities :\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;The bone marrow is involved and the possible etiological cause could be Multiple Myeloma.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThe kidney is involved and the possible cause of the patients problems could be AKI induced due to the myeloma.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThe lungs are involved due to tuberculosis and it makes the patient more susceptible to other infections.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EHematologically anemia is seen and it is mostly due to the Multiple myeloma and its pathophysiology.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThe following is the timeline of events :\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EInitially he started with Alcohol consumption and tobacco smoking for a period of about 35 years. Then he stopped binging on alcohol about 4 yrs back.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThen about 1.5 yrs back when he had complaints of fever, generalized weakness and anemia, about 2 units of blood were transfused into him .\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E4 months back he allegedly stopped smoking.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EHe's been complaining of low grade fever, generalized weakness, headache, neck pain, loss of appetite and weight loss since the last 2 months.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EHe's been having complaints of cough and SOB since the last 2 weeks.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EFinally he's complained of episodes of vomitings and pain abdomen since the last 2 days before admission in the hospital.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EFinal outcome was that after the prescribed treatment, the patient felt relief from his symptoms and was referred to an oncologist in view of further management of his condition.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EA2) Antibiotics were given to this patient for his underlying infection probably suspecting an atypical pneumonia.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EATT was given for his TB\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EWhere are the \ndifferent anatomical locations of the patient's problems and what are \nthe different etiologic possibilities for them? Please chart out the \nsequence of events timeline between the manifestations of each of these \nproblems and current outcomes.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EA1) The anatomical locations of the patients problems with the etiological possibilities are as follows :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EHis Heart is affected(HFrEF) mostly due to chronic DM and HTN which has probably lead to microvascular dysfunction subsequently leading to the heart failure.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003Ethe pedal oedema, SOB etc could also be due to Renal failure or hypoalbuminemia.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThe Seizures were mostly due to the right frontal lobe infarct. the stroke would most probably be caused by the AF.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThe following is the\u003Cb\u003E sequence of events\u003C\/b\u003E that lead upto the current time period were the patient presented with the complaints :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EHe initally started chewing tobacco about 40 yrs back\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThen 10 yrs back he started consuming alcohol. DM was diagnosed 7 yrs back and HTN was diagnosed about 5 yrs back.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EHis 1st episode of GTCS was about 3yrs back and he also suffered from AF with HFpEF then\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003Ehis 2nd episode of GTCS was 2 yrs back.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EHe suffered from HFrEF and anasarca 1 yr back which then subsided with medication\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EHe gradually developed pedal oedema 6 months back and now he he presented to the hospital with the complaints of increase in the pedal oedema, abdominal distension, SOb and decreased urine output since the last 3 days.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003ECurrent outcome was that his symptoms were relieved with the help of medication and he was discharged.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E \u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E1.LASIX :\n Mortality: 3 placebo-controlled trials (n=221) reported data; the OR \nwas 0.25 (95% confidence interval, CI: 0.07, 0.84, P=0.03), representing\n an absolute risk reduction of 8% in mortality in patients treated with \ndiuretics compared to placebo.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EWorsening\n of heart failure: 4 placebo-controlled trials (n=448) and 4 \nactive-controlled trials (n=177) reported data. The OR was 0.31 (95% CI:\n 0.15, 0.62, P=0.001) for the placebo-controlled trials and 0.34 (95% \nCI:0.10, 1.21, P=0.10) for the active-controlled trials.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK69174\/\" style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK69174\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E2.METAPROLOL : For HTN\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EUSE OF BETA BLOCKER IN HEART FAILURE:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EHeart\n failure is accompanied by increase activation of sympathetic activity. \nThis brings structural % functional modification in myocardium. Beta \nblockers inhibit the sympathetic outflow of norepinephrine and \ncounteract the changes. The ventricular remodelling in heart failure is \nalso reversed by beta blockers.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEjw4Zspz1huCGWwBw2NMhz-4rcpqkpJPwjZ5XoGtm30erm5TCyXXhIPgq-k7jPj4oB7XD2Bed1aGtySXiKdrbfKJJB1HGvfbxp4_ZkhyO02CZEsdGNLrE4kq5_dvzpj2tkA7lAnjd_p8_I\/s868\/hfb.jpeg\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E3.ENALAPRIL : For HTN \u0026amp; as afterload reducing agent for heart failure\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EP - In this \ndouble-blind trial, we randomly assigned 8442 patients with class II, \nIII, or IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EI\n - 8442 patients to receive either LCZ696 (at a dose of 200 mg twice \ndaily) or enalapril (at a dose of 10 mg twice daily), in addition to \nrecommended therapy.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EC- LCZ696 was superior to enalapril in reducing the risks of death and of hospitilization for heart failure.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"466\" data-original-width=\"1125\" height=\"266\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEjTyAAYoA43ztMU1RKShXepESwrZLLGUCWKaH27tuPrXvY_Y_KfPn53POlkYD2gENV7AHb-IPi56GLfEGV-gRDCeRfdBNTccbyc2vl7m6jguzlKzD94PEXQX8LjDCgjJHdSMFw-jmc0g1Y\/w640-h266\/enal2.jpeg\" width=\"640\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EO-\n 'A total of 711 patients (17.0%) receiving LCZ696 and 835 patients \n(19.8%) receiving enalapril died, of these patients, 558 (13.3%) and 693\n (16.5%), respectively, died from cardiovascular causes . As compared \nwith enalapril, LCZ696 also reduced the risk of hospitalization for \nheart failure by 21% and decreased the symptoms and physical limitations\n of heart failure. The LCZ696 group had higher proportions of patients \nwith hypotension and nonserious angioedema but lower proportions with \nrenal impairment, hyperkalemia, and cough than the enalapril group'.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.nejm.org\/doi\/full\/10.1056\/nejmoa1409077\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.nejm.org\/doi\/full\/10.1056\/nejmoa1409077\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E \u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E4.PHENYTOIN : For seizures \u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E5.H.ACTRAPID INSULIN : For DM\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E6.PREGABALIN : For neuropathy\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E7. tab ECOSPIRIN to prevent stroke\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EThis trial was randomized, double-blind and placebo-controlled.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EP\n - Patients with ischaemic stroke but not complete paresis were \nincluded. Totally, 441 patients (220 aspirin, 221 placebo) completed the\n trial.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EI - Tablets Aspirin 325 mg or placebo, water solvable, were administered orally once a day for five consecutive days.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003ENeurological\n assessments were carried out three times daily during the treatment \nperiod to detect progression of at least two points in the Scandinavian \nStroke Supervision Scale.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;Patient outcome was followed up at discharge and at 3 months\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EC - As regards patient outcome at discharge and after 3 months, aspirin treatment did not show any difference.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EO\n - Aspirin treatment did not significantly reduce the frequency of \nstroke progression. Amongst aspirin‐treated patients, stroke progression\n occurred in 15.9% as compared with 16.7% in the placebo group, which is\n less frequent than expected. The relative risk was 0.95 in the \ntreatment group.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThe Pedal oedema , SOB, scrotal and penile swelling is mostly due to heart failure and gauging from his history it seems to be caused by chronic alcoholism causing wet beri beri.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThe Axonal Sensory neuropathy can be said to be caused by the toxic effects of alcohol on the nerves and their myelin sheath due to free radical injury etc .\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThe sequence of events in the patients that lead to his present presentation :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EInitially the patient started consuming alcohol and khaini etc about 3 yrs back.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThen about 1 yr back he complained of pins and needles.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThe bounding palpitations were felt by him about 8 months back with complaints of PND about 3 months back and pedal oedema and SOB about 2 months back.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EFinal outcome was that he was completely relieved of his symptoms with medical management.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E \u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E \u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Q2) \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EWhat are the \npharmacological and non pharmacological interventions used in the \nmanagement of this patient and what are the efficacy of each one of \nthem?\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EA2) \u003Cb\u003EPHARMACOLOGICAL INTERVENTIONS :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E1.\u003Cb\u003ELASIX\u003C\/b\u003E :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EMortality:\n 3 placebo-controlled trials (n=221) reported data; the OR was 0.25 (95%\n confidence interval, CI: 0.07, 0.84, P=0.03), representing an absolute \nrisk reduction of 8% in mortality in patients treated with diuretics \ncompared to placebo.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EWorsening\n of heart failure: 4 placebo-controlled trials (n=448) and 4 \nactive-controlled trials (n=177) reported data. The OR was 0.31 (95% CI:\n 0.15, 0.62, P=0.001) for the placebo-controlled trials and 0.34 (95% \nCI:0.10, 1.21, P=0.10) for the active-controlled trials.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK69174\/\" style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK69174\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E2.\u003Cb\u003ETHIAMINE\u003C\/b\u003E :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EIn\n the study by Schoenenberger and colleagues (n=9), patients who took \nthiamine had 3.30% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.63%, 5.97%) greater \nLVEF compared to those on placebo.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003ELikewise,\n Shimon et al reported that thiamine resulted in 2.20% greater LVEF than\n the placebo group (n=29), although the extra improvement was not \nsignificant (95% CI: −18.97, 23.37%).\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003EIn\n our meta analysis, thiamine supplementation resulted in a significantly\n improved net change in LVEF (3.28%, 95% CI: 0.64%, 5.93%) compared with\n placebo.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3865826\/#:~:text=Compared%20with%20placebo%20(2%20trials,0.64%25%2C%205.93%25).\" style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3865826\/#:~:text=Compared%20with%20placebo%20(2%20trials,0.64%25%2C%205.93%25).\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E3.\u003Cb\u003ETELMISARTAN\u003C\/b\u003E : It was used to reduce the afterload that would aid his heart that was in a state of failure.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003ENON PHARMACOLOGIC :\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: georgia;\"\u003E1.SALT AND FLUID RESTRICTION :\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: 16px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 16px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 16px;\"\u003EA 35 year old gentleman from South India whos' a porter by occupation presented with a 2 month history of progressive bilateral pedal oedema and\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eand swelling of the scrotum and penis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 16px;\"\u003EHis earliest recollection of being absolutely normal goes back to days prior to the national lockdown, when he remembers he first developed heavy bounding palpitations, which he describes, \"as a ball kicking his chest from within\". The palpitations were often associated with dyspnea and sweating. They were initially intermittent, associated with exertion (lifting heavy weights) and relieved with rest for a few minutes. On probing further, he also recalled that twice in the last few months, he had to wake up from his sleep, feeling breathless and sweating profusely and felt a sense of \"air hunger\" and a need to seek fresh air. He reports that he used to walk on the road for an hour on so at 2 in the wee hours. Over the last two months his symptoms started becoming even more bothersome, as they were only intermittent earlier. On direct questioning, he reports an insignificant chest pain and a rare\u0026nbsp; nocturnal dry cough. He denies wheezing at any point. He also reported to us that the patient occasionally felt dizzy, with hollowing of vision and sweating during these episodes. He denies loss of appetite and involuntary weight loss.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 16px;\"\u003EOn targeted review of systems, the patient reports a nagging pins and needles sensation in his feet since 1 year, which has now ascended to his fingers. He denies numbness. The patient also told us that he had slippage of footwear for the past few months, which he gets to know quite a few seconds after they have slipped. He also reported difficulty in walking in the dark since a month. He cannot quite recall a significant muscle weakness in upper or lower limbs. \u003C\/span\u003E\n\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 16px;\"\u003EThe patient works as a cookie and has a significantly history of alcoholism - consumes 90 to 180ml of Officer's Choice, with frequent indulgences in \"Gudumba\", \"Sara\" and a good litre of toddy. His diet is fairly mixed and on occasions goes to bed without eating. His sexual life has taken a hit and he says he hasn't felt the same \"vigour\" over the last 3 months. He also frequently has to strain for defecation, which has been troubling him for 2 months now.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C!--\/data\/user\/0\/com.samsung.android.app.notes\/files\/clipdata\/clipdata_bodytext_201107_100754_481.sdocx--\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 16px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFinally being distressed by the state of his overall well-being, he came to the clinic for further evaluation and possible relief from all his symptoms.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EUpon General examination, the patient was conscious, coherent and was well oriented to time, place and person.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPallor was seen in the lower palpebral conjunctiva\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eand Quincke's pulse was seen under the fingernails\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ciframe allowfullscreen='allowfullscreen' webkitallowfullscreen='webkitallowfullscreen' mozallowfullscreen='mozallowfullscreen' width='320' height='266' src='https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/video.g?token=AD6v5dw8viEurWZmQJgh7szOJKk1xnt_P-PCyU7xs-oKr1mJB2zbMQXpDls53pAg-3JqabKfmmXpIV3591Z37RpTIQ' class='b-hbp-video b-uploaded' frameborder='0'\u003E\u003C\/iframe\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThere were no signs of icterus, cyanosis, clubbing and lymphadenopathy.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe penis and scrotum were markedly enlarged(13cm x 10cm for the scrotum).
